newsitem.title: JAPAN: Palladium seen supported at $120/oz -- Japan traders.
newsitem.headline: Palladium seen supported at $120/oz -- Japan traders.

text.p: Palladium prices may drift a bit lower after futures prices in both Tokyo and New York slumped to life-of-contract lows, but initial support at $120 per ounce in the spot market should be solid in the near term, Japanese traders said on Wednesday.
Some traders added that $120 was a level at which Almazjuvelirexport, the Russian export agency, was likely to intervene to prop up the market.
"Sentiment in the palladium market remains bearish with no bullish factors in sight, as the Japanese palladium market continues to face a chronic oversupply," a trading house trader said.
"But the chance that palladium will slip below $120 is fairly slim due partly to possible intervention by the Russian export agency," he said.
Japan is the world's largest consumer of palladium, which is used in automobile catalysts, mobile phones and a variety of electronic goods.

Traders said that domestic palladium inventories, estimated at about five tonnes, remained high and were declining only gradually, as demand growth in the semiconductor sector proved less than previously anticipated.
In New York on Tuesday, the NYMEX most-active December palladium contract hit a lifetime low of $123.75 per ounce.
TOCOM yen-based futures matched those declines on Wednesday, with benchmark August 1997 sliding to a lifetime low of 435 yen per gram before closing three yen lower at 436.
Spot palladium was quoted as low as $121.75 overnight before recovering slightly, and during Asian trading hours it was quoted around $122.50/3.50 per ounce.
"Palladium was supported by physical buying in Asian hours, but the buying momentum would not be enough to push up prices," one trader said.

Traders said the sharp drop in palladium prices in New York was attributable to selling from investment funds, based on views that palladium had been lagging behind recent falls in the other precious metals.

In Tokyo's spot market, palladium ingot prices have held nearly flat to world benchmark prices, or loco Zurich, since the end of last year, reflecting sluggish demand from Japan's electronics sector. Tokyo ingot usually trades at a premium of about $1.00 to $1.50 per ounce over Zurich.
In contrast to this, the price of palladium sponge, used in autocatalysts and other industrial applications, managed to maintain a modest premium over Zurich ingot of about $0.50 an ounce.
